World.title: Saudis Halt Oil Deliveries to Europe. What Does This Mean for Croatia?
World.content:
September the 17th, 2026 – Saudi Arabia has stopped oil deliveries to Europe following a drone incident, but what exactly does this mean for Croatia specifically?

Saudi Arabia has cancelled crude oil deliveries to European refineries after drone attacks damaged a key Saudi oil pipeline leading to the Red Sea. As a result, Europe’s largest buyers are urgently seeking replacement oil. Index/Neven Barkovic reports that hehind the halt in deliveries is the closure of the East-West pipeline, through which the Saudis transport millions of barrels of oil daily to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea in order to bypass the Strait of Hormuz. After the 10 September attack, which Saudi Arabia blames on Iraqi militias, the pipeline was shut down. Since 11 September, not a single tanker carrying oil has left Yanbu for Europe.

The interruption immediately created a major problem in Europe, which, after imposing sanctions on Russia over its invasion of Ukraine, has relied heavily on Saudi oil. At least three European refineries have been left without their agreed shipments for the end of September, with deliveries postponed as far as November. Polish oil giant Orlen, which covers around 40 percent of its needs with Saudi oil, is now rapidly buying stocks from the North Sea and the United States to keep its refineries in Poland, the Czech Republic and Lithuania running.

The market reacted to this disruption with a rapid rise in prices. While Brent crude futures are trading at around $108 per barrel, on the physical market in Europe the price of the benchmark barrel has reached as high as $122.

croatia has stocks… but they’re getting pricier

What does this mean for Croatia, specifically? There will be no physical shortages of oil at domestic petrol stations. Croatia supplies itself with crude oil by sea via the terminal in Omišalj and the JANAF system, sourcing it from various origins – from Mediterranean and North African to American. The domestic refinery in Rijeka is not directly dependent on the Saudi port of Yanbu in the way that refineries in northern and eastern Europe are.

However, expensive European oil will inevitably affect prices at Croatian pumps. Retail fuel prices in Croatia are calculated on the basis of quotations for petroleum products on the Mediterranean market (CIF Med). When the physical barrel price in Europe jumps above $120, this automatically raises Mediterranean quotations, meaning that in the next calculation cycle the input price of fuel for Croatia will be significantly higher.

can the government do anything?

Whenever fuel prices at the pumps rise significantly, citizens’ first question is – why doesn’t the state lower the levies? In every litre of fuel that drivers put into their tanks in Croatia, state levies – the fixed excise duty and VAT – make up more than a third of the total price. Croatia has a general VAT rate of as much as 25 percent, one of the highest in the entire EU, which is moreover calculated on the total amount after the excise duty has already been included. In other words, the state systematically charges tax on tax. As the price of the raw material on the exchanges rises, the budget automatically collects more and more money from VAT on every litre sold, without ministers having to lift a finger.

Although those in power regularly defend themselves with claims that their hands are tied by European directives on minimum excise duties and that they have already used the room for intervention, the real reason for refusing greater tax relief lies in the habit of filling the state coffers. Excise duties and taxes on energy products bring in hundreds of millions of euros of clean, secure and rapid revenue that the state uses to finance a huge public sector, the growth of the administration and political compromises.

cheap political manoeuvres and more and more money…

Any serious discussion about the state permanently forgoing part of that money is interrupted by the thesis of a “budget hole”, even though that shortfall could easily be made up by rationalising public spending, cutting unproductive costs and reducing the oversized state apparatus. Instead of taking that path, the authorities prefer to protect budget revenues at the expense of citizens’ living standards and the economy’s business operations.

That is why the Croatian Government has for years primarily relied on the cheapest political manoeuvre: pressure on distributors’ commercial margins. But margins make up only a smaller part of the final fuel price, and their administrative cutting pushes small private petrol stations towards the edge of profitability and creates the risk of some sales points closing. By shifting the burden onto traders and customers, the state retains its own lion’s share of every bill, while at the same time serving citizens the story that it is doing everything in its power. Economy Minister Ante Šušnjar justifies the rise in oil prices solely by the crisis around the Strait of Hormuz and global disruptions, claiming that the Government skilfully uses the tools at its disposal and that Croatia, despite the price rise, has the cheapest fuel in the region.

“Security of supply comes into question if exchange trends are not followed. Government decisions are balanced so as not to endanger security of supply, while still keeping petroleum products affordable,” Šušnjar said, repeating that Croatia has already used the EU exception and lowered excise duties below the prescribed European minimum. But the minister thereby conceals that with every new wave of price increases the state collects more and more money per litre through VAT, while in practice almost entirely shifting the burden of the crisis onto the backs of citizens and the cutting of distributors’ margins.

World.title: Autism Centre: 35 Million Euro Zagreb Project Gets Underway After 20+ Years
World.content:
September the 16th, 2026 – The long awaited Autism Centre is an enormous 35 million euro Zagreb project that is finally getting underway after a long 20+ year wait.

After over 20 years of announcements, the City of Zagreb has finally obtained a building permit for the construction of a new Autism Centre in Oporovec. It will provide modern and adapted conditions for learning, development and professional support for around 200 children, and will bring together programmes that are currently run at multiple locations across Zagreb.

Poslovni reports that the estimated value of the new Autism Centre in Oporovec is around 35 million euros, of which 19.3 million euros will be financed from EU funds through the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NPOO), while the remaining amount will be secured from the City of Zagreb budget. Once the building permit becomes final, the preparation of project documentation and the public procurement procedure for selecting the contractor will follow. Construction is planned to start in the summer of 2027, with a planned duration of 18 months.

The new school will have 48 classroom departments and educational groups, as well as three preschool education and care groups. Specialised spaces are also planned for music and art therapy, household skills and aquatic therapy with a pool, sports halls and other facilities adapted to the needs of users.

According to the project by the architectural office SODA-ARHITEKTI, the centre will cover more than 9,600 square metres on three floors, with 60 parking spaces, nine of which are designated for people with disabilities. Attention has also been paid to the outdoor landscaping, with a main square featuring a sensory park, fountains and facilities for developing motor skills planned. “This is another of the projects that have been promised in Zagreb for more than twenty years, and now it is finally going into realisation,” said Zagreb Mayor Tomislav Tomašević.

Deputy Mayor Danijela Dolenec stressed that the new school will represent a major step forward in the quality of spatial and programmatic conditions for the education and upbringing of children and young people with autism. The Autism Centre currently cares for around 300 users through preschool programmes, primary education, full-day and half-day stay programmes, and organised housing, she said.

Dolenec added that the City of Zagreb continues to invest in the existing capacities of the Autism Centre. A public procurement for the renovation and arrangement of the sports hall in Ljevakovićeva Street, worth 250,000 euros, was recently launched, and around 750,000 euros has been invested in the renovation of the Centre’s existing facilities in recent years.

By the end of the year, the opening of a new Centre space in Juraj Dalmatinac Street is also planned, where early developmental and psychosocial support services will be provided for 40 children, as well as a stay programme for 30 adults with autism spectrum disorders. The City of Zagreb has also stated that 24 new special classroom departments and educational groups have been established in the new school year, increasing existing capacities by almost a quarter.

The number of special classroom departments has grown from 64 back in 2021 to 126 in 2026, while the network of schools implementing these programmes has been expanded to 55 schools across Zagreb, according to the City of Zagreb press release.

World.title: Zadar Mobile Boat Pharmacy is in the Final for the Best EU Project Award
World.content:
September the 16th, 2026 – The very commendable Zadar mobile pharmacy on a boat is in the final for the Best EU Project Award.

The Zadar project “Mobile Pharmacy – boat for the islands of Zadar County” has secured a place in the final of this year’s competition for the best EU project in the category Contribution to the Local and Regional Community. Morski reports that this very commendable initiative is primarily aimed at introducing a mobile pharmaceutical service in the island area in order to significantly facilitate residents’ access to medicines and professional advice, especially those in more traffic-isolated places.

The competition is organised by the Croatian Association of Counties, the Office of the European Parliament in Croatia and the portal Župan.hr, under the auspices of the Ministry of Regional Development and EU Funds. In strong competition from almost 50 projects submitted from all over Croatia, the expert jury selected a total of 36 finalists, with the Zadar mobile pharmacy competing among the 18 best in its category.

The winners in the readers’ choice category are decided by the public, and public voting officially ran from the 8th to the 15th of September, 2026.

World.title: Croatia to Get Most Modern Thermal Spa in Historic €42 Million project
World.content:
September the 16th, 2026 – Croatia is set to get its most modern and largest thermal spa as a historic 42 million euro project finally nears completion.

Works on Wellovar in Veliki Korenovo, the largest construction project in the history of Bjelovar worth €42 million, have entered the final stage. Poslovni reports that the enormous complex with a total of ten pools is already taking on its final appearance, and finishing works and system checks are currently underway before opening. Bjelovar Mayor Dario Hrebak regularly visits the construction site and emphasises that the focus is now on the details and on balancing and calibrating one of the most complex and modern heating, cooling and hot water systems in Croatia.

“Works on the largest thermal spa in Croatia, our Wellovar, are nearing completion. Only minor details remain, but this is one of the most complex and modern heating, cooling and hot water systems in Croatia. We now have to ensure that the entire system is balanced and calibrated. It is hard to say when we will open the doors. Our great wish is that it will be on the 29th of September, on the Bjelovar City Day, but it is very difficult to predict,” said Hrebak. He added that at this moment the exact opening date is not crucial; the most important thing is that the project is completed to a high standard.

“What matters is that everything we see is heading towards its final stage and that the people of Bjelovar will get a standard that 95 percent of other cities in Croatia do not have. Croatia will also get an excellent centre for the development of water sports,” he stressed. In addition to tourist and recreational facilities, Wellovar is also expected to play an important role in the development of sport. According to Hrebak, the facility has been designed to meet the standards for hosting national and international swimming and water polo competitions. “We are truly looking forward to it soon opening its doors and delighting our citizens, as well as all tourists and visitors with its facilities,” Hrebak concluded.

With the completion of this massive €42 million project, Bjelovar is set to gain a major new sports, recreational and tourist complex. Although the official opening date has not yet been confirmed, the city administration’s wish is for Wellovar to welcome its first visitors as early as the 19th of September, on Bjelovar’s City Day.

World.title: Croatia to Make Changes to ENC Usage as of March 1st, 2027
World.content:
September the 16th, 2026 – Croatia will make significant changes to ENC usage as of March the 1st, 2027, and drivers with multiple vehicles need to pay particular attention to what is coming.

The much anticipated new Croatian road toll collection system will use ENC technology, but also automatic licence plate recognition via cameras. Poslovni reports that for years now, ENC has been one of the simplest ways to pay motorway tolls across Croatia. You put the device in your car, drive through the marked lane, and the system automatically handles the payment. However, with the introduction of the new electronic toll collection system, one thing becomes much more important than before: the ENC will also be linked to the vehicle’s registration plate.

From the 1st of March 2027, when the new system starts operating, the vehicle’s registration number, data on the ENC device, and a valid means of payment will have to be registered in the system for the ENC model to be used. The law expressly stipulates that a driver using ENC must pass through the toll point in a vehicle whose registration plates are identical to those linked in the system to the ENC device in the vehicle. This means it will no longer be enough simply to take a working ENC device and put it in any car. Before driving, it will be important that the vehicle being used on the motorway is properly registered in the new system.

this is particularly important if you use one enc for multiple cars

The change is especially significant for those who currently use the same ENC in several cars. Under the current rules of Croatian Motorways, an ENC device for vehicle categories IA, I and II is not tied to a single registration number. It can be used in multiple vehicles of the same category, provided the same device is not used simultaneously in more than one vehicle. The new system introduces a different principle: the registration number becomes an integral part of the data linked to the ENC device. Therefore, drivers who currently simply move the ENC from one car to another will have to make sure that the registration of the vehicle they are using is correctly linked to the device in the Electronic Toll Collection System.

The law itself does not currently stipulate that one ENC can necessarily be linked to only one registration number. The detailed rules on use and changes to data will be regulated by the rules of the new system. However, it is clear that the previous practice of simply transferring the device without checking the registration will no longer be sufficient. The good news for existing users is that current ENC devices will not become unusable. The law obliges motorway operators to include ENC devices purchased before the establishment of the new system into the new ESNC no later than its start.

the new cameras will read license plates

The new toll collection system will use ENC technology as well as automatic licence plate recognition via cameras. For passenger cars and other light vehicles, drivers will be able to choose between the ENC model and a model based solely on the registration number and a registered means of payment. When using ENC, the system will therefore have data on both the device and the vehicle’s registration number. Cameras will record the vehicle’s passage and read the licence plates in order to identify the vehicle and verify payment. For drivers, this brings a new habit: before driving, it will no longer be enough simply to check whether the ENC is in the car and whether there are sufficient funds on the account. They will also have to make sure that the vehicle’s registration number is correctly registered in the system. This is precisely what could be particularly important for those who currently use one ENC in multiple cars.

World.title: Iraq appoints new ambassador to US
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s new Ambassador to the United States, Krikor Der-Hagopian, officially presented his credentials to US President Donald Trump on Tuesday during a formal ceremony at the White House.

According to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry, Ambassador Der-Hagopian’s mission aims to keep track of the outcomes of Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s visit to the United States, working to build a new chapter in Iraqi-American relations, broadening strategic ties, and expanding political, economic, investment, and security cooperation to strengthen Iraq’s regional role and serve the interests of both countries.

Der-Hagopian will work on advancing the economic, investment, energy, and security memoranda of understanding established during al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington in July.

The appointment of the new ambassador marks an important shift in Baghdad’s diplomatic strategy. As an Armenian Christian, Der-Hagopian is the first non-Shiite envoy sent by Iraq to Washington in modern history.

Der-Hagopian was educated in Denver, Colorado, and has prior experience working with former President Barham Saleh and former Prime Minister Mohamed Shia al-Sudani.

Foreign policy analysts see Der-Hagopian’s selection as a clear indication that Iraq is prioritizing highly skilled, strategic trust-builders to handle Baghdad’s relationship with Washington.

Der-Hagopian follows diplomat Nizar al-Khairallah, who has held the position since June 2023.

World.title: Iraq stores oil in facility in Kirkuk to raise exports via Turkey’s Ceyhan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has initiated a trial operation to transport crude oil using tanker trucks from its southern oil fields to a storage facility in Kirkuk, an effort that aims to enhance oil supplies destined for the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

This initiative is part of a broader Iraqi effort to increase oil flows through the northern export route after the US-Israeli war against Iran disrupted Iraqi shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, the country’s main export channel.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, said that the ministry has reached a deal with Iraq-based KAR Group to transport crude oil using its fleet of tanker trucks. This arrangement was confirmed in a statement issued by the state-owned Basra Oil Company (BOC).

BOC stated that the trial operation began on September 13 and lasted two days, during which slightly over six million liters of crude oil, equivalent to about 38,000 barrels, were transported on 209 tanker trucks, each with a capacity of 30,000 liters.

According to Oil Ministry estimates, current oil flows from northern Iraq to the Turkish port of Ceyhan are believed to be around 200,000 barrels per day, a decrease from roughly 250,000 before the Iran conflict.

According to BOC sources, the project faces logistical obstacles such as a shortage of tanker trucks and inadequate loading facilities in the southern oil fields. The initial volumes remain too small to allow for a significant increase in exports from north Iraq.

World.title: EBRD boosts trade financing in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is bolstering trade financing in Iraq by extending a credit ceiling of up to US$ 25 million (€21.3 million) to Bank of Baghdad, one of Iraq’s main private-sector banks.

The initiative is part of the EBRD’s Trade Facilitation Program (TFP) and aims to assist the Bank of Baghdad in enhancing its import and export transactions, as well as expanding its correspondent banking relationships.

The funding will assist in closing trade financing gaps in Iraq, improve access to trade finance for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) involved in cross-border trade, and boost commercial ties with regional and worldwide markets.

The technical cooperation funded by the EBRD will include advising help, specialized training, access to the EBRD Trade Finance e-Learning Program, and seminars on essential trade finance subjects.

The European Union will fund the creation of a dedicated training curriculum for the Bank of Baghdad, focusing on core and advanced banking competencies, improving staff skills, strengthening service delivery, and promoting the continued development of Iraq’s banking sector.

The initiative will also promote financial inclusion by providing a specific training module on increasing access to financial services for underrepresented populations, particularly women.

The Bank of Baghdad is one of Iraq’s top three private banks, with total assets of $2.2 billion by the end of 2025 and 35 branches around the nation.

In 1999, the EBRD launched the TFP initiative to enhance international commerce. The program provides guarantees and short-term loans to selected participating banks, which in turn support local exporters, importers, and distributors.

World.title: Iraq, Turkey finalize draft transport infrastructure agreement
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Transport Ministry announced on Friday that Iraq and Turkey have finalized an agreement regarding the development of transport infrastructure.

The agreement paves the way for official government recognition and a formal signature.

The deal was reached after a memorandum of understanding was reached by Iraqi Transport Minister Wahab al-Hassani and Turkish Transport and Infrastructure Minister Abdulkadir Uraloglu in late July.

Officials from both sides completed the document after four days of intense discussions in Baghdad.

The agreement formulates a comprehensive institutional framework to regulate cooperation in developing infrastructure projects and modernizing transportation systems.

The draft framework includes a program to implement various phases of the Development Road, a strategic project proposed by Iraq to transport goods and energy from Basra to Turkey, in accordance with the approved technical priorities, timelines, and project completion requirements.

Given the economic and developmental importance of the Development Road project to Iraq and the region, this step serves as a critical foundation for consolidating Iraqi-Turkish cooperation and organizing joint working mechanisms.

The move is part of Iraq’s efforts to upgrade the transport sector and boost investment opportunities and economic integration, supporting strategic projects and strengthening Iraq’s position as a key hub for transport, trade, and regional and international supply chains.

World.title: Where the US-China tariff row stands ahead of White House summit
World.content:
Beijing – Trade frictions between the world’s top two economies are set to take centre stage next week when US President Donald Trump hosts Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping at the White House.

Although a shaky truce was reached last October that halted the frenzied escalating tariff battle launched by Trump, a comprehensive and permanent deal has remained elusive.

Here is where things stand ahead of the summit, which is expected to take place on September 24:

How high are current levies?

Tariffs have represented a major hurdle in the China-US trade relationship since 2018, during Trump’s first term.

In April 2025, the base US tariff rate on Chinese goods reached an eye-watering 145 percent — matched by China’s reciprocal levies of 125 percent — although both sides have since significantly reduced rates.

Tolls are now imposed by both sides in a complex patchwork of sector-specific policies.

The effective tariff rate for imports from China, which balances various duties paid across all items, was 22.8 percent as of July, the highest among all major US trading partners, according to research organisation the Penn Wharton Budget Model.

Among the highest effective tariff rates for Chinese goods heading to the United States are 40.5 percent on steel and aluminium, it said.

China still maintains a 10 percent levy on all US goods, with additional rates applicable in other specific sectors, such as 15 percent on liquid natural gas.

How much is still being traded?

Trade between the world’s two largest economies has continued despite the turbulence caused by the tariffs.

Total imports and exports hit $400.8 billion in January through August this year, Chinese customs data shows, a 5.4 percent rise from the same period in 2025.

But the balance is lopsided, with Chinese exports accounting for 75 percent of that.

Beijing’s soaring trade surplus has long ruffled feathers in Washington, while a similar asymmetry with the European Union is also exacerbating tensions with Brussels.

What is being discussed?

Trump told reporters on Sunday that he would be discussing “almost everything” with Xi at the summit.

Tariffs, however, are “the main issue on the agenda”, Dan Wang, a director on Eurasia Group’s China team, told AFP. “Xi wouldn’t go if there were no deliverables on tariffs or a trade truce,” she said.

Beijing and Washington are currently in consultation about a tariff reduction framework covering $30 billion worth of products on each side, China’s commerce ministry said last week.

That goal was agreed at Xi’s last meeting with Trump in Beijing in May, during which they also agreed to establish trade and investment councils intended to manage friction.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday that he will meet his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng this weekend for talks expected to lay the groundwork for the White House summit.

What is China’s leverage?

Beijing successfully pressured Washington to back down from its sky-high tariffs last year after imposing stringent controls on exports of rare earths, the critical minerals used for various high-tech products whose processing is dominated by China.

“China still has the upper hand” going into next week’s talks, said Wang of Eurasia Group.

The country’s supply chains are “very flexible”, and its historic boom in exports has not been significantly dented by tariffs so far, she noted.

Xi’s diplomatic clout has also been on full display recently, having met this month with several leaders including Russian President Vladimir Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, traveling to Bishkek, Cairo and New Delhi.

What is Trump seeking?

With global oil prices spiking following renewed fighting in the US war with Iran, the Trump administration is looking to allay concerns about the economy ahead of crucial midterm elections in November.

Securing Chinese guarantees to purchase US agricultural goods, particularly soybeans, has been a recurring objective in trade talks with Beijing.

The meeting will also give Trump the chance to project statesmanship while hosting a high-stakes diplomatic engagement at the White House — Xi’s first visit to the US capital in 11 years.

What are other potential pitfalls?

Several other fraught issues threaten to derail any sweeping agreement.

Beijing’s economic and diplomatic support for Tehran is one major sticking point, with recent reports by the Wall Street Journal claiming that Chinese entities supplied Iran with satellite imagery of a military base housing US troops in Jordan.

Fierce technological competition is also ongoing, particularly in the closely watched artificial intelligence sector.

The US government last week accused Chinese AI labs of stealing the capabilities of US firms on an “industrial scale”.

World.title: Most stocks rise as Fed hikes and indicates drive to curb inflation
World.content:
Hong Kong – Most equities rose Thursday after the Federal Reserve hiked interest rates for the first time in three years and boss Kevin Warsh sounded a hawkish note that ramped up bets on another increase as officials fight surging inflation.

Investor sentiment was also given a lift by hopes for a pick-up in oil supplies from Saudi Arabia after the country moved to restore some capacity from a pipeline it closed at the weekend following drone attacks.

In a unanimous decision, the Fed lifted borrowing costs for the first time since 2023, defying President Donald Trump’s demand for cuts, as Warsh stressed the need to combat inflation that has been “too high” for “too long”.

“We removed a dose of accommodation so that financial and credit conditions would be more consistent with our ultimate objectives,” Warsh said after the announcement.

“Today’s action starts to show we’re serious about this, and we will deliver on the price stability objective.”

The decision was announced along with a graph showing the vast majority of Fed policymakers saw at least one more was likely necessary before the end of the year.

Traders now see an October hike as being a 50:50.

While Wall Street’s three main indexes ended Wednesday in the red, Asian traders took the 25-basis-point lift more positively, with analysts saying it shored up credibility in the central bank and provided some reassurance over officials’ determination to beat inflation.

Long-term government bond yields — which this week touched two-decade highs — fell as investors pared back their inflation expectations, which at 3.4 percent is currently well above the bank’s two percent target.

“Removing a dose of accommodation is not the language of a central bank that believes it has completed the job,” said Stephen Innes at Quintex Intel.

“It suggests policy was still providing support before Wednesday and may not yet be restrictive after it.

“The hike removed the immediate credibility question. The explanation created a new argument about how much tightening remains.”

And Christian Scherrmann at DWS added: “Overall, we believe the main motivation this time was credibility, given bond market pricing and recent developments in oil markets.”

Still, he added: “Despite his hawkish stance, Fed Chair Warsh’s optimistic outlook on the economy may be music to many ears.”

Equity markets across Asia were mostly higher in early trade.

Tokyo, Seoul, Singapore, Taipei, Wellington and Jakarta all advanced, though Hong Kong and Shanghai dipped.

However, Tai Hui, of JP Morgan Asset Management, warned: “We think the chance of U.S. policy rates returning to above five percent is still limited.

“Nonetheless, a catalyst to extend the equity bull market (lower interest rates) is looking unlikely in the foreseeable future.”

The news angered Trump, who called Warsh a “good man” who had “a hostile board”.

“They’re raising the rates to make Trump do as bad as they can possibly do… So they’re raising that only for political reasons, and that’s a raise against Trump,” he complained.

While the Middle East crisis continues to weigh heavily on sentiment and oil prices above $100 a barrel, investors took some cheer from reports that Saudi Arabia is looking to return about half the capacity of its cross-country oil pipeline within days.

The East-West conduit was shut last week after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis targeted it.

State-run Saudi Aramco said it was looking to get back up to full capacity in about six weeks, Bloomberg cited sources as saying.

The news sent crude prices tumbling around three percent Wednesday, and they extended the losses Thursday.

The Fed hike and Warsh’s remarks also pushed the dollar higher against its peers and held the gains in early trade.

Eyes are now on decisions by the central banks of Britain and Japan, with the latter also expected to hike as it looks to fend off a rise in inflation and a weaker yen.

World.title: US again denies Palestinian leader Abbas visa to attend UN assembly
World.content:
Washington – The United States has denied Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas an entry visa to attend the UN General Assembly in New York next week, a source familiar with the case said Wednesday.

In a separate statement that did not mention Abbas by name, the State Department say it would deny visas to members of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) and officials with the Palestinian Authority (PA), “as a consequence of their failure to reform, contrary to their commitments to the United States, and their ongoing activities that undermine the prospects for peace.”

A source familiar with the matter confirmed to AFP that the Palestinian Authority president, Abbas, was covered by the measure.

The Trump administration took the same step last year, forcing the Palestinian leader, a regular at the UN General Assembly, to address the body of global leadership by video.

In its statement Wednesday, the State Department said that the PLO and PA had “once again, failed to live up to their commitments.”

“This includes initiating and supporting actions at international organizations that undermine and contradict prior commitments,” the department also said.

Washington also accused the organizations of “taking actions to internationalize the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict including through the International Criminal Court (ICC) and International Court of Justice (ICJ), seeking to bypass negotiations through seeking unilateral recognition, and continuing to pay stipends to terrorists and to glorify acts of terrorism and terrorists in public pronouncements and school textbooks.”

The move puts the United States at odds with numerous countries, including France, that recognized a Palestinian state at the United Nations last year.

A total of 142 UN member states endorsed it following the conference on a two-state solution co-chaired by France and Saudi Arabia.

The decision comes as violence by Israeli settlers against Palestinians has escalated in recent months in the West Bank.

Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967, and violence there has surged since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack that triggered the war in the Gaza Strip.

According to an AFP tally based on Palestinian health ministry data, Israeli soldiers or settlers have killed at least 1,109 Palestinians in the West Bank — fighters and civilians — since October 7, 2023, when a Hamas-led attack killed more than 1,200 people.

The ensuing Israeli military campaign waged relentless strikes on Gaza that have killed more than 73,700 people, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

The international community has expressed concern over the violence, but the United States has remained largely quiet on the issue, saying only that the US government opposes any annexation of Palestinian territory.

World.title: AI looms large ahead of Xi, Trump summit
World.content:
Washington – Artificial intelligence is set to loom large when Chinese President Xi Jinping meets counterpart Donald Trump in Washington next week, but for all the urgency surrounding the technology, the rivals remain far from agreeing on anything substantial.

The United States and China are the two dominant powers in the AI race, and officials and analysts describe the technology’s future starkly, as a world shaped by one superpower’s AI or the other’s.

China, long seen as trailing the United States on frontier AI, has been closing that gap fast.

Chinese firms including DeepSeek and Moonshot AI have released open-weight models — which anyone can download, modify and run — that now rank just behind the top closed US systems from OpenAI and Anthropic, at a fraction of the cost.

Moonshot’s Kimi K3, released this summer, is seen by analysts as the clearest sign yet of that narrowing gap.

Washington has long tried to slow China’s progress with export controls on the advanced chips needed for cutting-edge AI, blocking access to top-end US semiconductors such as Nvidia’s.

The Trump administration has eased licensing rules for some chips even as it moves to restrict others, to the frustration of China hawks in Washington who want a harder line.

The AI question became more urgent after the recent Hugging Face incident, in which OpenAI models broke out of a test environment, triggering global alarm over the technology’s fast advancement — and calls for the industry to slow down or pause development.

– ‘Lose the race’ –

The AI debate in the US remains dominated by the idea that the country’s leading developers — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta — cannot afford to slow their pace of innovation, whatever the risks, for fear that China will pull ahead.

“If Congress just races in and does some sort of emergency session to try to regulate AI, we will lose the race to China, and that is a threat to every single American,” House Speaker Mike Johnson said this week.

Trump has taken a starker line, accusing AI safety advocates of bad faith and raising the specter of China dominating the field.

“There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China,” he wrote on his Truth Social platform.

Unease about AI’s danger to geopolitical standing is also alive in Beijing.

Minister of State Security Chen Yixin on Sunday described AI as “the main battleground” for global competition “and a new track for major power strategic rivalry.”

Despite the heated rhetoric, hope remains that the two global rivals can agree on something regarding the technology when the leaders meet in Washington.

But anything ambitious, like agreeing to slow development or craft global safeguards, is likely out of reach.

The US and China are stuck in “a prisoner’s dilemma at two levels,” said Aalok Mehta of the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), arguing that neither individual AI labs nor individual countries can afford to slow down unilaterally as long as they fear their rivals will not.

“What would it mean if the US were to slow its pace at a time China doesn’t?” asked Jennifer Huddleston of the Cato Institute, framing the dilemma facing US policymakers.

“What does that mean for our allies who are going to be looking to find technological solutions from someone” other than China, she added.

– ‘Close communication’ –

Others were skeptical that even modest cooperation was likely.

Jonathan Czin of the Brookings Institution said the dim prospects for cooperation reflect divisions on both sides.

“There’s not a consensus, by any means, that’s crystallized in the United States on what, if anything, to do about AI,” he said.

On the Chinese side, he said, there is “a deeply ingrained suspicion” that any dialogue on restraint is “just going to be a trap” designed to slow China down.

Any deal would likely be hammered out ahead of time by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who meets his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng this weekend to prepare the ground.

“As the number one and number two superpowers in AI by a lot, it behooves all of us to put up guardrails, to have close communication,” Bessent told reporters this month.

World.title: 'If I open my mouth': Decoding deepening fault lines between allies-turned-rivals - Akhilesh Yadav & Jayant Choudhary
World.content:
and Jayant Choudhary were once allies. Now, every exchange between them seems to make their fallout a little more bitter and also personal.

Their ongoing face-off touched a new low this week after Jayant unleashed another strong attack on his former ally.

"When we had an alliance with them, we knew many things, but all those details are not supposed to be shared.

It is my âgravityâ that I donât talk about those things. If I open my mouth and share all those details, he wonât find space to even stand in Uttar Pradesh," Jayant warned Akhilesh.

The RLD chief's angry reaction came after he was asked about Akhileshâs remarks on number of seats Jayant should get to contest in the 2027 assembly elections as part of the BJP-led NDA.

Akhilesh, who has often targeted Jayant ever since they parted ways in 2024, had mocked the RLD's current standing within the NDA and suggested that the BJP should give it many more seats than what it got under SP alliance if it truly respected the legacy of Chaudhary Charan Singh, Jayantâs grandfather and former Prime Minister.

Jayant hit back strongly and accused Akhilesh of making "light remarks."

Jayant countered Akhileshâs remarks

Jayant also tried to turn the Chavvani jibe against Akhilesh and said: "PDA (which refers to backwards, dalits and minorities) plank of Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav was aimed at reaching out beyond the party's traditional vote bank, but people would also judge on how much respect and unity the party had maintained with its earlier supporters.â





The RLD allies once again came out strongly in support of Jayant and attacked the SP leadership.

Chief minister Yogi Adityanath led the counter-attack on behalf of Jayant and termed the SP chief's comments an "insult to democracy". He accused Akhilesh of making a "mockery of democratic discourse" by resorting to cheap language against political opponents. The UP CM also labeled Akhileshâs remarks as an insult to the entire farming community and the legacy of former Prime Minister Chaudhary Charan Singh.

Other UP ministers also jumped to the defence of Jayant Choudhary.

The latest exchange comes after an ugly war of words last month triggered by Akhilesh Yadavâs âchavanniâ jibe at Jayant over walking out of the SP alliance ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and joining the BJP-led NDA.

The 'chavanni' story

The origins of Akhileshâs Chavanni jibe go back to January 2022. Jayant, who was then allied with the Samajwadi Party, was asked about attempts by the BJP to bring him into its camp.

"Main koi chavanni hoon jo palat jaunga" (I am not a 25 paise coin that will flip), Jayant had said then. But two years later, the âchavvaniâ did flip.

Jayant slammed Akhilesh

Ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the RLD walked out of its alliance with the SP and joined the NDA. This happened after the Modi government conferred the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honor, posthumously to former Prime Minister Chaudhary Charan Singh in February 2024, months before the Lok Sabha elections.

At a recent event, the SP chief recalled Jayantâs political switch and said: "Jaane kahan-kahan se aa gaye the log gathbandhan banane. Humne chavanni ka rupya bana diya tha, tab bhi humein chhod kar chale gaye wo. (âPeople from all sorts of places had come to ally with us. We had raised their political worth from a âchavanniâ to a full rupee, yet they left us and walked away.â)."

Akhilesh did not take names, but the reference was obvious.

Jayant had reacted strongly to Akhileshâs jibe and accused the SP chief of making 'cheap' remarks. âIf he wanted to attack me politically, he should have taken my name directly instead of making indirect references,â Jayant had then said.

The RLD chief had then received strong support from his allies, with the BJP coming out in his defence. Even BSP chief Mayawati backed Jayant. They quickly turned Akhileshâs attack on Jayant into an attack against Choudhary Charan Singh, the farmers and the Jat community.

Battleground Western UP

So, why is Akhilesh targeting Jayant? Is he still trying to settle political scores for the RLD chiefâs betrayal in 2024? Or is Akhilesh trying to drive a wedge between RLD and BJP ahead of the assembly elections?

Akhilesh knows that the stakes are high for all political parties in Western Uttar Pradesh. With the RLD no longer on his side, the SP chief plans to go all out to strengthen its presence in the region ahead of the 2027 polls.

Jayant Choudhary, meanwhile, has been trying to broaden the RLDâs social base and extend his partyâs areas of influence in Uttar Pradesh. This is important for him to show his clout within the NDA. Western UP, with its sizeable Jat, Muslim and farming communities, has traditionally been an important electoral battleground for Jayant and RLD.

The politics in the region is already beginning to get tense. Last week, Akhilesh had to cancel his Western UP outreach in the region after a party meeting planned in Bulandshahr could not be held.

The local administration, citing waterlogging, refused permission for landing of his chopper. The SP alleged that the waterlogging was an "excuse" and that the BJP-led government was behind the denial.

The SP reacted by announcing that the party will organise a series of rallies in Western UP, beginning from Bulandshahr. "Sometime later this month, the national president will visit Bulandshahr and he will also tour every district of western Uttar Pradesh.

Saharanpur will also be included in the programme in due course," senior SP leader and party spokesperson Rajendra Chaudhary said.

"The public is watching and understanding everything. When the time comes, they will teach the BJP a befitting lesson," he said.

Saharanpur is also expected to figure in the SP's upcoming political outreach. The district has recently witnessed a political and legal controversy following the demolition of a mosque structure in the collectorate premises.

So, the SPâs aggressive pitch against Jayant could be part of its political offensive to dominate the region.

Why is Akhilesh speculating RLD seats?

Is Akhileshâs ploy of linking RLD seats to the legacy of Choudhary Charan Singh an attempt to drive a wedge between Jayant and the BJP?

When Jayant contested the 2022 assembly elections with Akhilesh, the RLD had got 33 seats as part of the SP alliance. Now, by linking seats for RLD to Chaudhary Charan Singhâs legacy, Akhilesh could be trying to pile pressure on both Jayant and the BJP when they sit to negotiate a workable formula to divide seats, especially in Western Uttar Pradesh, where RLD has a strong presence.

But will this work? Political analyst J P Shukla says no. âIf Akhilesh Yadav hopes to gain from trying to create differences between RLD and BJP, he is not going to succeed. It is now too late for any major political realignment. By now, they would have settled most of the issues among them,â Shukla says.

Shukla terms these political face-offs as an attempt by leaders to keep their cadres engaged and energised for the political battle.

Senior political analyst Anand Vardhan Singh says Jayant would not mind the attention from the war of words with Akhilesh. âHis strong remark against Akhilesh is posturing for a greater share of seats. And to that extent, the confrontation with Akhilesh helps,â he says.

Singh says Jayant has little room to manoeuvre as most of the Jats would stay with the BJP even if the RLD chief decides to leave the NDA.

Explaining Akhileshâs attacks, Anand Vardhan Singh says, âAkhilesh is desperate for Dalit votes and would not mind being branded anti-Jats.â

Could Akhilesh end up helping Jayant?

While Akhilesh may be stepping up his political attacks on Jayant to push him on the back foot, the SP chief should be wary of his strategy being counterproductive. His remarks have already prompted BJP leaders to rally behind Jayant Choudhary. From chief minister Yogi Adityanath to several UP ministers, BJP leaders have hit back at Akhilesh, presenting his attacks on Jayant as an insult to Chaudhary Charan Singh, farmers and the Jat community.

Even BSP chief Mayawati came out openly in support of the RLD chief after the Chavvani face-off. Mayawati condemned Akhilesh Yadav and sought his apology.

"The public statement made by the Samajwadi Party (SP) chief regarding his former ally party, the Rashtriya Lok Dal, and its leader, the Union Minister--that "Hum logon ne chavanni ko rupaiya bana diya, phir bhi chhod ke chale gaye"--is utterly indecent, unbecoming, and extremely shameful.

For such arrogant and undemocratic rhetoric, he should immediately apologize not only to that party and its leader but also to the entire Jat community for insulting the family of the late Chaudhary Charan Singh Ji; that would be appropriate," wrote Mayawati in an X post.

For the RLD, the attacks may end up doing more good than harm. They give Jayant Choudhary another opportunity to underline his political relevance in western Uttar Pradesh and, in turn, strengthen his hand when the NDA sits down to work out its seat-sharing formula for 2027. If that happens, Akhileshâs attempts to put Jayant on the defensive could very well boomerang.

World.title: Film scenes with drug consumption, trafficking to carry anti-drug warning label
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Films depicting consumption or trafficking of drugs will now carry an anti-drug warning, the broadcast ministry notified on Wednesday.

According to the guidelines amended under the Cinematograph Act, such movie scenes will carry the warning: "Illicit Narcotics Destroy Health and Guarantees Imprisonment.

Say No to Drugs".

The move follows a similar direction issued to OTT platforms by the ministry last month, asking them to prominently display the same warning during scenes showing the consumption or use of narcotic drugs. A similar advisory was also issued to private satellite television channels.

The latest change marks a departure from the earlier film certification guidelines, under which the

(CBFC) was required to ensure that scenes that could "encourage, justify or glamorise drug addiction" were not shown.

However, those guidelines did not mandate a specific warning to be displayed on screen.

The film certification guidelines set out the principles that the CBFC must follow while examining films for public exhibition under the Cinematograph Act. They were last amended in May 2025, when the government added three age-based parental guidance categories â U/A 7+, U/A 13+ and U/A 16+. Introduced through amendments to the Cinematograph Act in 2023, the categories require parental guidance for children below seven, 13 and 16 years, respectively.





The guidelines also require the CBFC to ensure that anti-social activities, including violence, are not glorified or justified, while criminal methods that could encourage offences are not depicted. They also prohibit scenes that encourage, justify or glamorise drug addiction.

World.title: 'Your leadership has transformed India into a world power': Netanyahu greets PM Modi on 76th birthday
World.content:
Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday extended birthday greetings to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, describing the India-Israel relationship as an âunprecedented partnershipâ and saying the friendship between the two countries had ânever been strongerâ.

Birthday greetings poured in from across the world, with foreign leaders, envoys and diplomatic missions highlighting Indiaâs bilateral partnerships and Modiâs role in strengthening ties. Russian president Vladimir Putin praised his contribution to the âspecial and privileged strategic partnershipâ between India and Russia, while Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni wished Modi âhealth, energy, and successâ.

âHappy birthday, Narendra!â Netanyahu wrote in a post on X, alongside an image of the two leaders. âYour leadership has transformed India into a world power. Together, we have built an unprecedented partnership between our two great democracies.â

The Modi-Netanyahu bonhomie has become a prominent feature of India-Israel ties, with both leaders repeatedly highlighting their personal friendship and political trust.





Their meetings and public exchanges have highlighted a relationship that extends beyond formal diplomacy into close strategic cooperation.

âThe friendship between Israel and India has never been stronger, and together we will take it to even greater heights,â he added, wishing Modi âmany more years of leadership, health and fulfillmentâ.

India and Israel established full diplomatic relations in 1992, while PM Modiâs July 2017 visit to Israel elevated the relationship to a strategic partnership.

Netanyahu followed with a visit to India in January 2018.

The relationship now covers defence, security, technology, agriculture, water, innovation, trade and other areas. During PM Modiâs visit to Israel in February 2026, Netanyahu described him as âmy dear friendâ and said, âYou are more than a friend; you are a brother in many respects.â He also said, âIsrael is stronger than ever and India is stronger than ever.â

Netanyahu's birthday message came days after India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, where the grouping adopted a New Delhi Declaration that included strong references to the Israel-Lebanon conflict and the Gaza war.

On Lebanon, BRICS leaders said, âWe welcome the ceasefire in Lebanonâ and called for full implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701. The declaration also called on Israel to âwithdraw its occupying forces from all of the Lebanese territories, in which they remainâ.

World.title: 'It can't be that Hindi will not be taught in Tamil Nadu', SC tells state during hearing on Navodaya schools
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Tamil Nadu government to comply with its December 15, 2025 order to identify land in every district for establishing Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas, while urging the state and Centre to resolve their differences over the schools through dialogue.

A bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and Augustine George Masih also questioned Tamil Nadu's opposition to the three-language policy followed by Navodaya schools and said the state should not view the establishment of the centrally funded institutions as a threat to its existing education system.

"You have to change your mindset, it canât be that Hindi will not be taught in the soil of Tamil Nadu," Justice Nagarathna observed during the hearing.

The bench also said the people in Chennai should not alienate those in Delhi while stressing the need for cooperative federalism.

"We are saying in addition to all the good things youâre doing in your State, having something in addition will not bring down your standards. Coming from Delhi, will not lower the standards of Chennai. People in Chennai should not alienate Delhi and vice versa," the Court said.

The court granted Tamil Nadu three more months to identify suitable land in each district and directed representatives of the state and Central governments to hold further discussions on the policy for establishing the schools.





The matter has been posted for December 14.

Tamil Nadu raises language concerns

The case relates to Tamil Nadu's challenge to a Madras High Court direction to establish Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district.

Navodaya schools are centrally funded, co-educational residential schools run by the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti under the Union Ministry of Education. Tamil Nadu has opposed their establishment, among other reasons, because the schools follow a three-language policy that includes Hindi, while the state follows a two-language policy.

Senior Advocate Jaideep Gupta, appearing for Tamil Nadu, told the court that the state's objection was not to schools or the teaching of Hindi as such, but to the language policy associated with the Navodaya scheme.

"It is against the State policy. It supersedes Tamil. This kind of unification is not the purport of the Constitution. It is not a Central government school. It is a school run by a society. There is an adamancy that Hindi must predominate."

Justice Nagarathna said the language issue could be discussed between the Centre and the state.

"If you want Tamil as a second language, it is a matter which can be considered," the Judge said, asking the state Secretary to speak to the corresponding Central government Secretary.

Gupta said discussions had already taken place but the Centre had remained adamant about Hindi. He nevertheless agreed to another round of consultations.

Court stresses cooperative federalism

Tamil Nadu also argued that the judiciary could not compel a state to adopt an optional Central government policy through a mandamus.

Gupta submitted that education is in the Concurrent List and that Tamil Nadu has constitutional authority to frame its own education policy. He also argued that the Navodaya scheme was not compulsory.

Justice Nagarathna questioned the consequences of individual states refusing to accept Central policies.

"Education is in the Concurrent List. There has to be cooperative federalism. If each State says that I don't accept your policy, what will happen?" the Judge asked.

The bench said Tamil Nadu could continue running its own institutions and following its own syllabus, while Navodaya schools would provide an additional educational option.

The court also rejected the argument that the establishment of Navodaya schools would lower Tamil Nadu's educational standards.

"We are not alienating you and we are not alienating them. Some more type of schools come in your state also which will only enhance the high standard which we are aware of. This is not going to lower your standards. If Navodaya schools were going to lower the standard of education in Tamil Nadu we would have said that irrespective of what you would have said. That is not the case here. It will provide more opportunity," Justice Nagarathna told Gupta.

"Ultimately everybody must work together," Justice Nagarathna said.

State raises financial concerns

Tamil Nadu also raised financial concerns, submitting that the Centre had promised to release Rs 5,000 crore for education but had not done so.

Gupta argued that the state could not take on additional financial liabilities when funds under existing schemes had allegedly not been released.

Additional Solicitor General KM Nataraj, appearing for the Centre, submitted that the state's primary requirement under the scheme was to provide land, while construction and other expenses would be borne by the Central government.

Nataraj said the scheme was at an early stage and construction would take several years, during which the language-related differences could be addressed through discussions.

Gupta, however, said around 30 acres of land would be required in each district and that identifying land before deciding whether to accept the policy would create difficulties.

The bench clarified that it was not directing the state to acquire land immediately, but only to identify suitable land in its government plan.

Supreme Court refuses to recall land direction

The Supreme Court had in December 2025 directed Tamil Nadu to identify land required for establishing Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district within six weeks. The state subsequently sought recall of the order.

On Thursday, the bench declined to recall the direction and instead granted the state three months to comply.

In its order, the bench recorded that Tamil Nadu had cited the change in government and lack of material progress in discussions with the Centre as reasons for non-compliance.

"Be that as it may, we direct the petitioner to comply with our order of 15.12.2025 in so far as identification of the land necessary to establish the school in each district," the order stated.

The bench also directed the Centre and Tamil Nadu to continue discussions on the policy while the state works on identifying the land.

Advocates G Priyadarshini and Rahul Shyam Bhandari, appearing for Kumari Maha Sabha, the petitioner before the High Court, argued that Tamil Nadu could not deny students access to free education through Navodaya schools.

"The Court should not get into this debate," Gupta said during the hearing.

Justice Nagarathna responded: "That perception that you are surrendering to the central govt should not be there."

World.title: Govt debunks Pakistan claim that IAF MiG-29 crashed during landing due to pilot error
World.content:
âPakistani propagandists run video game footage as IAF crash

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The press information bureau (PIB) fact check unit on Thursday debunked a social media claim that an Indian Air Force (IAF) MiG-29 fighter jet had crashed during landing due to pilot error. They stated that the video being circulated was footage from a video game.The fact-checking unit warned that the video was being circulated by Pakistani propaganda accounts and called the claim fake.âPakistani propaganda accounts are circulating a video with the claim that an IAF MiG-29 fighter jet crashed during landing due to pilot error,â PIB Fact Check said in a post on X, adding, âBeware! This claim is #Fake.âThe unit said the footage was from War Thunder, a military combat video game featuring aircraft, land and naval vehicles.The video circulating on social media shows a fighter jet crashing while attempting to land, followed by the pilot ejecting and parachuting to safety. The footage was presented online as an actual IAF MiG-29 crash by certain accounts based out of Pakistan.PIB Fact Check urged users to report suspicious content related to the Government of India through its official channels.The claim is part of a recurring pattern of propagandist accounts circulating unrelated military accidents and video-game footage are circulated as evidence of recent events.

World.title: 'Tell your Chief Secretary not to invite orders’: SC pulls up Manipur over 25 unnatural deaths in relief camps
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Manipur government to submit a comprehensive report on 25 unnatural deaths of internally displaced persons reported in relief camps during the 2023 ethnic violence, including an alleged sexual assault case.

A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana questioned the state over the limited number of post-mortem examinations conducted in the cases and the compensation paid to the families of the deceased.

The court directed the state to provide details of all 25 cases, including post-mortem reports and other documents establishing the causes of death.

âTell your Chief Secretary not to invite orders. Tell us what measures you have taken,â CJI Surya Kant remarked while questioning the Manipur Advocate General about information sought by the committee on July 4.

Supreme Court seeks details of deaths

The proceedings took place while the court was hearing petitions related to the investigation and trial of sexual violence cases arising from the 2023 Manipur ethnic violence.

The bench took note of a report submitted by a committee headed by former Jammu and Kashmir High Court Chief Justice Gita Mittal. The report referred to the deaths in relief camps and raised concerns regarding compensation.

The court sought an explanation from the state on why post-mortem examinations had reportedly been conducted in only 20 of the 25 cases and why the families had received compensation of only Rs 20,000 to Rs 30,000.





The report placed before the Supreme Court also referred to 640 deaths in relief camps across eight districts.

Directions on FIRs and relief camp conditions

The court directed the Manipur government to explain the remedial measures taken to protect the safety and dignity of internally displaced persons living in relief camps and to ensure adequate medical facilities and day-to-day necessities.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The Manipur Legal Services Authority was directed to immediately take up the issue and ensure registration of FIRs in all cases of unnatural deaths, proper ascertainment of the causes of death and expeditious investigation.

It was also directed to take measures for the protection of displaced persons and victims.

The Supreme Court's directions come against the backdrop of the ethnic violence that erupted in Manipur in May 2023, which led to deaths, displacement and allegations of sexual violence.

World.title: Internal roads in pathetic condition across Hyderabad
World.content:
Roads dug up and left unattended to for months in colonies across the city are testing the patience of vehicle riders by slowing the movement of traffic.

While the ire of the city residents about the condition of main roads is visible all over the social media, little attention is paid to the condition of internal roads, which is going from bad to worse over the past one year.

Major infrastructural works, such as laying of the stormwater pipelines as part of the Strategic Nala Development Programme, and drainage lines, has left several stretches bumpy and unmotorable.

A case in point are the colony roads in Tarnaka, between Lalapet and Nacharam main roads, which were dug up for laying of pipelines, but not re-carpeted. The stretch continuously witnesses two wheeler and four wheeler traffic to and from Lalapet, which calls for immediate repairs.

“This stretch was never hassle free since I had known. It was either speed bumps, or sunken manhole covers, or vehicles parked on the side which hamper the ride. Now, it has become worse, the whole stretch has become unnegotiable. My car swings like it is on a ship,” says Srinivasa Ramakrishna, a regular commuter.

The RTC Colony main road and colony roads around it in Chintalkunta too have been heavily dug up, but not re-carpeted for several months. Absence of local area representatives since the dissolution of the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation’s council has not helped the matters.

“The road is very busy here, and vehicles bouncing over the road even at low speeds could be dangerous, because it’s challenging task for the driver to steer around. The road turnings have become especially difficult for two vehicles in opposite directions,” shared Mohd. Quadri, an auto driver from the Jahangir Nagar Colony.

Similar complaints are shared from areas such as Hitech City, Gachibowli, Attapur, Rajendranagar, Nizampet, Bachupally, and other areas.

“Every internal road is damaged, dug up and looks like a war zone — went to Madhapur-Kakatiya Hills, Ayyappa Society and Gayatrinagar yesterday — total neglect. Just cosmetic touches for some main roads,” posted Kishore, a user on the social media platform X.

“I’m writing this post out of frustration and and curiosity. Why Hyderabad roads are digging [dug up], wherever you go you can see a patch. Entire Hyderabad looks like that. In some areas after digging they are not even properly repairing. Can someone tell me why they doing like that?” posted a Reddit user.

World.title: Pakistan announces austerity measures amid rising fuel prices
World.content:
Pakistan on Thursday (September 17, 2026) announced a raft of austerity measures to curb fuel consumption as escalating conflicts in West Asia led to an increase in global oil prices, threatening nationwide gas and power supplies.

The measures, approved by the Pakistan cabinet, will remain in effect for three months as the government seeks to contain fuel consumption and expenditure.

The development comes after the government on Tuesday (September 15, 2026) raised the price of petrol by PKR 4.10 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) by PKR 6.41 per litre, taking them to PKR 384.34 and PKR 415.83 per litre, respectively.

Also Read | Pakistan mulls revival of austerity measures amid West Asia hostilities

Oil prices have risen amid continuing tensions in West Asia and concerns over supplies following attacks on energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including the temporary closure of its East-West oil pipeline after an aerial attack.

Under the measures announced on Thursday (September 17, 2026), fuel allocations for government vehicles will be cut by 50%, although vehicles used by the armed forces, law enforcement agencies and essential services will be exempted.

Markets will be required to close by 9 p.m., while marriage halls can operate until 10 p.m. and restaurants until 11 p.m. Drug stores and medical laboratories will be exempted from the restrictions.

The government also announced a 5% reduction in non-employee-related expenditure and banned official foreign visits as well as domestic travel for meetings, asking officials to switch to virtual meetings instead.

Official dinners have also been prohibited, except those hosted for foreign visitors and delegations, while the purchase of new government vehicles has been banned.

World.title: At least 15 ZPHS students in Sangareddy take ill after lunch
World.content:
At least 15 students of Zilla Parishad High School in Pedda Loni village of Munpalle mandal, Sangareddy district, fell ill after lunch on Thursday.

All the students are stable and have been kept under observation. A teacher who ate the same food as the students reportedly experienced severe symptoms and was shifted to the Government Hospital in Sangareddy.

According to preliminary information, the food was brought from outside and was not part of the school’s mid-day meal programme. The students began experiencing symptoms such as vomiting and stomach pain, and the school staff rushed them to the Community Health Centre in Sadashivpet, where they were administered first-aid and electrolytes.

World.title: Five arrested in Sivaganga double murder case
World.content:
Sivaganga police have arrested five persons in connection with the recent murder of two men in the district.

Police said Deyvendiran, 25, was from Kayaodai Pudukudiyiruppu near Kalaiyarkovil in Sivaganga district. He ran a bar at Pollachi in Coimbatore district. Having come to his hometown, he bought a new car. Two days ago, he and Poovandi, 25, from Siruvelangudi, who worked at a private financial institution, went to Kodikkad kanmai (tank) near Sivaganga in the car. They sat near the tank and consumed alcohol.

An eight-member gang arrived on two-wheelers and chased the two men. The gang members hacked them to death and damaged Deyvendiran’s car before fleeing the scene. Sivaganga Town police registered a case.

Based on the orders of District Superintendent of Police Abhishek Gupta, five special teams led by DSP Amal Edwin were formed. Based on CCTV camera footage and cell tower data, the special teams arrested five persons in connection with the murder. They were identified as Balamurugan, 24, Dhanaraj, 19, and Santhosh, 19, all from Billur near Sivaganga, Sathishkumar, 25, from Mathur and Kaleeswaran, 23, from Alupillai Thangi.

Meanwhile, the relatives of the victims staged a road blockade in front of Sivaganga Palace, refusing to receive the bodies and demanded the arrest of the real culprits, a compensation of ₹50 lakh each to the families of the deceased, and government jobs for family members of the victims.

Since the blockade lasted for over three hours, buses were diverted. Though police held talks with them, they refused to accept the body.

Relatives of the deceased said that some people had come for a function. They sat and consumed alcohol at the spot where the murder took place. A clash broke out among them at the time. Those who were attacked brought their supporters. By then, the attackers had left. At the moment, the two deceased individuals were consuming alcohol

“Seeing a gang heading towards them, both tried to run. That gang chased and hacked them to death. This is what they state for the reason of murder,” they added.

“However, that is not believable. How could both be killed simultaneously in a case of mistaken identity? Therefore, we plan to continue our protest until the real culprits are arrested.” they said.

Police said they were continuing the investigation and the motive could be established only after arresting the key culprits.

World.title: BJP stages protest in Hubballi over alleged curtailment of Vande Mataram
World.content:
Alleging that the Congress government had disrespected Vande Mataram by limiting its rendition to two stanzas, members of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) staged a protest in Hubballi on Thursday.

BJP workers and leaders from the Hubballi-Dharwad East Assembly constituency took out a procession from the Tuluja Bhavani Temple to the Mini Vidhana Soudha. The protesters raised slogans against the State government and demanded that Vande Mataram be sung in its entirety at official programmes.

The protestors alleged that restricting the national song to two stanzas amounted to disrespecting the song and demanded action against the Congress government for not allowing its full rendition.

BJP leaders submitted a memorandum addressed to the Union government through the Tahsildar, seeking that the entire song be sung at official functions.

Party workers and leaders from the Hubballi-Dharwad East constituency participated in the procession.

BJP leader Jayateertha Katti was among those who took part in the protest.

World.title: Man accused of killing pregnant wife stabbed to death in Nizamabad, revenge motive suspected
World.content:
A 27-year-old man, who was out on bail after being arrested for allegedly murdering his pregnant wife a year earlier, was ambushed and stabbed to death with a coconut-shelling knife by a gang in Nizamabad on Thursday evening. Police suspect the attack to be a pre-planned revenge killing.

The victim, Chittari Haribabu, was attacked at around 5 p.m. at Raja Rajendra crossroad. An officer from the Nizamabad police said that the assailants are yet to be identified and investingation is on to ascertain whether the murder was linked to the death of his wife Vaishnavi, a YouTuber, for which he had earlier been arrested.

Haribabu had been staying with his mother at Indrapur, under the limits of Nizamabad’s V Town Police Station, for the past few days. The two were making a living by selling maize bags at the crossroad.

On Thursday evening, Haribabu was went to a nearby shop for water when he was attacked. The assailants arrived in a car. “There were about three people in the car and one of them got down, approached Haribabu and attacked him with a coconut-shelling knife,” informed the officer.

The victim suffered severe injuries and died on the spot. CCTV cameras in the area captured the attack. Footage of the incident, which has also been circulating on social media, purportedly shows an assailant stopping the car on the opposite side of the road, with one of them rushing towards Haribabu and attacking him repeatedly with the sharp weapon. He was allegedly attacked around nine times before the man ran back into the car and they fled the place.

Police reached the spot following information about the murder and shifted Haribabu’s body to the Government General Hospital mortuary for post-mortem examination.

Investigators are now looking into old enmity as a possible motive, particularly Haribabu’s alleged murder of his wife Vaishnavi about a year ago.

Vaishnavi, a YouTuber from Madhapur village in Korutla mandal of Jagtial district, was married to Haribabu. She was four months pregnant when she was killed.

Haribabu had allegedly slit her throat with a knife and also attacked her hands and forehead. Following a complaint from Vaishnavi’s father, police registered a case and arrested Haribabu. He was subsequently released on bail.

World.title: Tirupati police gear up for ‘Garuda Seva’ rush, impose traffic curbs
World.content:
Tirupati is bracing for a major influx of pilgrims for the ‘Garuda Vahana Seva’ in Tirumala on Saturday, with the district police rolling out an extensive security and traffic management plan to ensure the smooth movement of devotees and vehicles during the high-footfall event.

The arrangements, drawn up in coordination with the district administration, Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD), vigilance wing, APSRTC and other departments, include traffic diversions, designated parking zones and dedicated transport to Tirumala.

Private vehicles will face restrictions, with devotees advised to opt for APSRTC buses and TTD vehicles. Dedicated parking facilities have been created for two-wheelers, four-wheelers and tourist buses at multiple locations in Tirupati. APSRTC buses will ferry pilgrims from these parking areas to Tirumala, with services available round the clock.

Two-wheelers will not be permitted on the Tirupati-Tirumala ghat road from 9 p.m. on Friday to 6 a.m. on Sunday. Parking for two-wheelers has been arranged at Balaji Link Bus Stand, Nehru Municipal Ground, SV Medical College Ground and ISKCON Ground.

Tourist buses will be accommodated at designated parking areas at Devalok, Trident and Mango Market on Zoo Park Road, while four-wheelers can be parked at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, Alipiri Link Bus Stand, SV Medical College Ground and SV Engineering College Ground.

Traffic diversions will be enforced for buses entering Tirupati from Chittoor-Madanapalle, Chennai-Puttur and Kadapa-Srikalahasti routes. Special arrangements have also been made to ensure unhindered movement of ambulances, fire engines and other emergency vehicles.

District Superintendent of Police L Subbarayudu urges devotees to follow the restrictions and traffic advisories, and cooperate with the police to ensure the safe and orderly conduct of Garuda Seva.

World.title: CPI(M) condemns preventive arrests of leaders in Kakinada
World.content:
The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] State unit on Thursday condemned the preventive arrests and proposed binding-over cases against CPM and mass organisation leaders and activists in Kakinada district for allegedly supporting an agitation by unemployed youth.

CPI(M) State secretary V. Srinivasa Rao stated in a release that the police had arrested Kakinada City CPM leader Palivela Veerababu, student leader M.G. Suribabu, youth leaders T. Raja and Adarsh, threatened to book them under binding-over proceedings.

He termed the police action undemocratic and alleged that the government was violating citizens’ fundamental rights by resorting to binding-over cases.

Mr. Rao said the leaders had been called to the police station and threatened with binding-over cases, describing the move as an attempt to suppress democratic dissent. He called upon people to condemn what he described as “authoritarian” measures and demanded the immediate release of those arrested.

World.title: Markets to close at 9pm as govt reintroduces austerity measures for fuel conservation
World.content:
The federal government reintroduced austerity measures on Thursday in an effort to conserve fuel amid renewed tensions in the Middle East, setting 9pm as the time for closing markets and reducing fuel provision for official vehicles by 50 per cent for a period of three months.
